While I don't typically have a knack for horror games, I really enjoyed this one!!! No jumpscares, chase sequences, or gore, though you may get startled a couple times because of a sudden loud noise or visual effect. The style of horror isn't about suspense and adrenaline; but unfamiliarity, curiousity, and a bit or exestentialism. You can't die, (yes there is a good reason why that's the case, but it's revealed towards the end of the game, and I'm not going to spoil anythin [: ) but you can get scared. No matter how much the spirits try, all they can do, is warn you. You want to explore the cave. Even though you can't see, you must explore it. The unfamiliarity of your surroundings mocks you, taunting you to explore and to travel deeper into the cave. You rediscover the forbidden knowledge, and yet you will crave more. It's almost as if knowledge is layed out like breadcrumbs, leading you into a big trap. You are aware of this possibility, but what's there to lose? You could go back to the safety of your tent, but no. You've already come this far. Knowledge, (like garlic bread), is extremely tasty. No cost is too great. It. Must. Be. OBTAINED. The real horror only settles in once the credits roll. You don't really piece together what's happening during the game, but that feeling of figuring everything out and having the world come together is amazing,  The story really comes together about 3/4 of the way through, but doesn't really exist before that. Scanner Sombre is a great recommendation for those who want to try a horror game, without the risk of becoming too scared or stressed, but still want to feel some good horror.

Gameplay:
Creative and enjoyable gameplay, even if it stays somewhat stagnant throughout the game. (There is actually a reason that the gameplay is the way it is, though it spoils the story). The burst scan is really satisfying and fun to use. The geometry of the areas are very detailed, and they look gorgeous when you take the time to fill the surfaces. The game is a rather linear affair, and there are no hidden collectibles on the side as far as I am aware. Granted in game collectables would not work given the gameplay, so it's understandable why there are none. 
I wouldn't recommend playing this game all in one sitting, but two or three sitting because you begin to feel cross eyed after a few hours. Also, since you are going to be scanning 90% of the time, the game might get a bit monotonous.
Sound design is impeccable. You feel like you are in scanner sombre. I do not think I have felt that immersed in a game since the metroid prime games + mario galaxy 1&2. The music is also great. It always fits the mood. 

Biggest criticism:
It is one of those games that can only truly be played once. While you can replay it, it won't have the same impact as it did the first time. Exploring the cave for the first time and discovering its secrets is what makes the game truly memorable. But once it's been discovered, that's that. Then again, it is only 8 dollars, so I'd say it's worth it despite it's lack of replayablity.
